newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina's Fernandez denies deficit exaggerated.
newsitem.headline: Argentina's Fernandez denies deficit exaggerated.

text.p: Argentine Economy Minister Roque Fernandez denied suggestions from his predecessor on the weekend that he exaggerated budget deficit projections to "scare legislators" into passing proposed tax increases.

In an interview with La Nacion published Saturday, former Economy Minister Domingo Cavallo said he doubted Fernandez's estimate that the deficit would reach $6.6 billion this year unless Congress approved his revenue-boosting measures. Cavallo speculated the figure was used to "scare legislators" into fast approval of the package.
The budget deficit was $2.5 billion in the first half.
The $6.6 billion deficit estimate "was not produced with the strategic intention to to pressure anybody, it is the reality of the numbers," Fernandez told Radio America Saturday.
In an interview with La Nacion on Sunday, Fernandez countered that Cavallo was overly optimistic in his assumptions for the second half of this year.
Cavallo had forecast five percent economic growth in 1996, while the ministry under Fernandez now predicts that will be closer to three percent.

"He was too optimistic about the recovery and the increase in tax collection," Fernandez said. "These forecasts will not be realized because economic activity was not as strong as predicted and expectations about better avoiding tax evasion were not met."
